display_name: Income Tax Ordinance s 66, separate calculation for spouses: who may claim it, where each spouse's income goes, property income under (b), the credit points s 66(c) gives in a separate calculation, and the common-source gate of (d)

run.method: one session working alone from BRIEF.md, per the encoding-a-subject skill; no sub-agents; no independent test pass

language.note: Every module starts @lang en; identifiers are English. Hebrew source strings are quoted in comments, copied from the deposited file.

source.note: Unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval. Hebrew is authoritative.

tax_years: From 2024. The last amendments to s 66 (תשפ״ג־6, תשפ״ד־3) apply from tax year 2024 per ITA circulars 2024-000012 and 2024-001090 (NOTES.md sections 3 and 7). From 0.2.0 every rule that takes the couple, or a tax year, refuses a tax year before 2024, because the earlier text is not in the source bundle; in 0.1.0 only three rules did (independent finding V-4, inventory 02-V4). Rules that take no year (one spouse, one item, a child's age, a provision) state the deposited text. A tax year after 2026 is a projection of the text as at 2026-10-06.
scope: s 66 in full: (a)(1)-(3), (b), (c)(1), (1A), (2), (3), (4) with (a), (a1), (4A), (5) with (a)-(c), (6), (d)(1)-(2); spent text ((c)(4)(b)-(d), (c)(5A), (e)) carried as inert stubs. Incorporated and encoded: the paragraphs of the s 1 definition of income from personal exertion (as an enumeration) and the s 40(b)(3) definitions of year of birth and year of majority. NOT encoded, taken as inputs or GIVENs: s 65 (the consolidated calculation is named as an outcome, not computed), s 64B (who is the registered spouse), the counts under ss 34, 35, 36, s 37's conditions, the value of a credit point (s 33A), the tax on income from personal exertion (ss 121 ff.), and the classification of income. From 0.2.0: s 48A, not encoded, is declined by name where it reaches the half point under s 36A that s 66(c)(4) gives (a woman who is a foreign worker), in row IL-01's words; s 66's own date edges (the (a)(1) five-year window, the (b) one-year and inheritance conditions) are the caller's.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source. An independent test pass was run after deposit by fid-il-02 (commit 240a478: tests-independent.l4, DECIDED-ANSWERS.md, INDEPENDENT-FINDINGS.md); from 0.2.0 one of its 103 assertions fails (E-4, line 385, fork F19, waiting on a ruling). No adversarial refuter has been run. The encoder's own assertions were written by the encoder (0.1.0) and the repair agent (0.2.0), from the source, so they share their readings; 23 of them transcribe the Israel Tax Authority's own published tables.

expected_red.why: The independent tester's module. E-4 (line 385, inventory 02-E4) expects a refusal for a 2024 calculation of a child born in 2023 with the mother's (a1) election set; the encoding keeps 5½ (fork F19, reading (i)) until Meng rules (BACKLOG IL-24). Listed in check.sh (expected_failed 1). V-4 (line 204), which also failed in 0.1.0, passes from 0.2.0.

forks.F1: s 66(d)(1): the common-source gate read as on the COUPLE (subsection (a) does not apply to them at all), not on the common-source income alone, which s 64B(b) suggests.
forks.F2: s 66(a)(1) proviso: a sum on commuting a pension (s 1 def. para (6)) is not a 'קיצבה'.
forks.F3: s 66(a)(2): equal non-zero incomes from personal exertion are answered by neither sentence; the encoding refuses.
forks.F4: s 66(a)(2): the comparison uses each spouse's whole income from personal exertion, including a pension the (a)(1) proviso keeps out of the separate calculation.
forks.F5: s 66(a)(3): 'ילדו' is the registered spouse's own child; a child of the other spouse alone is not reached.
forks.F6: s 66(a)(3): s 65's exception for assets from inheritance or bodily-injury compensation is not applied.
forks.F7: s 66(b) proviso: only the (a)(1) calculation of the spouse who is not registered is 'other income for which a separate calculation is made'; the registered spouse's claimed (b) income is always calculated alone.
forks.F8: s 66(c)(1A): not shut by the (d) gate, which names subsection (a) only.
forks.F9: s 66(c)(4)-(6): 'the woman' and 'the man' presuppose a mixed-sex couple; the encoding refuses for a couple of the same sex.
forks.F10: s 66(c): a credit provision it does not name (39A, 39B, 40A-40D, 44, 45, 46, ...) is refused, not defaulted.
forks.F11: s 66(c)(4)(a1): the birth-year election is the mother's and does not reach a step-mother's points under (4A).
forks.F12: s 66(c)(4A), (6): only a widowed partner's children count, not a divorced partner's.
forks.F13: s 66(c)(1A), (4), (5): the children's credit is capped at the tax on income from personal exertion; the ½ under s 36A is not.
forks.F14: s 66(a)(3) income stays on the registered spouse and does not move with the (a)(2) pool.
forks.F15: s 66(a)(3): a child who turns 18 during the tax year is outside it.
forks.F16: s 66(c) governs both spouses' calculations once (a)(1) gives a separate calculation.
forks.F17: s 66(c)(4), (5): no maintenance or custody condition on the children.
forks.F18: s 66(c)(1A): 'בן זוג' includes the registered spouse.
forks.F19: s 66(c)(4)(a1) at the vintage boundary (0.2.0, 02-E4; WAITS ON MENG, BACKLOG IL-24): a birth-year point elected in 2023 and carried into a 2024 calculation. (i) the 2024 text governs and the point lands, 5½ (taken by construction in 0.1.0, kept as the default); (ii) whether a 2023 mother could elect and had the point is 2023 law, not held: refuse (the independent tester's E-4). The election input carries no year.
